def: A table layout with one variable per column, one observation per row and one table per type of observational unit.
A table held in memory with labelled columns, each stored as an array; pandas' main data structure.
A column or set of columns that identifies each row of a table uniquely.
Two layouts of the same data: wide has one column per value of a variable (such as month), long has one row per observation.
A special number such as -999 used to mean 'missing' that parses as ordinary data unless it is found and converted.
A join that keeps only the rows whose key matches in both tables.
A join that keeps every row of the left table and fills the right-hand columns with NULL where there is no match.
The multiplication of rows when a join key is not unique in one table, which inflates counts and sums.
A row whose reference to another table (such as a user id) has no matching row there.
A SQL function that computes a value over a set of related rows without collapsing them into one row.
SQL's marker for an unknown value, which is not equal to anything, including another NULL, and is skipped by aggregates.
A data problem that compounds silently through a pipeline and appears late as a failure downstream.
